input.quote: 7.7 If any invoice is not paid within ten days of its due date, Customer shall pay Vendor, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount equal to fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week the invoice remains unpaid.
input.rationale: Section 7.7 imposes liquidated damages payable by Customer (15% of annual Fees per week of delay), which breaches the preferred position of no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer and is punitive in scale (it can exceed the remaining contract value within months, and applies even to short delays or disputed invoices notwithstanding Section 7.3). No early-termination fee exists elsewhere (Section 9.4 limits Customer to accrued Fees), so the fallback three-month cap is unnecessary. We replaced the LD with ordinary late-payment interest on undisputed invoices. Service credits payable to us and the mutual cap in Section 21 raise no issue.

ops.oldText: 7.7 If any invoice is not paid within ten days of its due date, Customer shall pay Vendor, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount equal to fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week the invoice remains unpaid.
ops.newText: 7.7 If any undisputed invoice is not paid within thirty days of its due date, Vendor's sole remedy is simple interest on the overdue amount at the lesser of one percent per month or the maximum rate permitted by Applicable Law, accruing from the due date until payment. Customer owes no liquidated damages, penalty, or similar sum under this Agreement.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We removed the 15%-per-week liquidated damages on late payment, as our playbook does not permit liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer, and replaced it with ordinary late-payment interest on undisputed amounts.
proposal.summary: Delete Customer-payable liquidated damages in 7.7 and substitute simple late-payment interest.
